title: An authenticated API request, end to end
summary: One POST from the browser through every middleware in registration order to Postgres and back, with the refusal each gate can issue instead.
note: The stack is drawn in Express registration order (apps/api/src/app.ts:31-71), because position is what decides reachability: anything registered above the gate at app.ts:62 answers without a session. The two Cloud middlewares (workspace resolution and the entitlement gate) are no-ops unless VITAE_CLOUD_ENABLED is set, which .env.example:40 leaves false, so in a default build the request goes straight from the auth gate to the router and the legacy real/demo space from spaceMiddleware is the partition. POST /api/v1/nodes is drawn as the concrete route; every other authenticated route passes the same stack.

actors.label: Browser
actors.note: One typed client sets every outbound header: bearer token or session cookie, x-vitae-space, x-vitae-tz (apps/web/src/lib/api.ts:57-60).

actors.label: requestContext
actors.note: Assigns or echoes x-request-id and logs one structured line per response. Registered first so it observes everything, including refusals.

actors.label: cspNonce + helmet + cors
actors.note: Per-request CSP nonce, Helmet headers, and an explicit CORS allow-list built from WEB_ORIGIN, never an origin reflector.

actors.label: express.json
actors.note: Two parsers: 15 MB scoped to /api/v1/imports, then the 2 MB default. Registration order is the whole mechanism.

actors.label: space + timezone context
actors.note: cookieParser, then two AsyncLocalStorage contexts: the data partition and the IANA timezone from x-vitae-tz.

actors.label: authGate
actors.note: Default-deny, mounted at /api. Everything registered above it answers without a session.

actors.label: workspaceMiddleware + entitlementGate
actors.note: Cloud only. Both return immediately when cloudEnabled() is false, which is the default build.

actors.label: v1Router → nodes route
actors.note: Thirty-three mounted prefixes; the route validates and orchestrates.

actors.label: Repository
actors.note: The only layer that turns a record into a row, and the only place the workspace filter is applied.

actors.label: Postgres
actors.note: One pool per process, statement_timeout 30s, TLS verified against an explicit CA on any remote host.

actors.label: errorHandler
actors.note: Registered last. Every thrown error leaves as one envelope shape.

steps.label: POST /api/v1/nodes with session, x-vitae-space, x-vitae-tz
steps.note: Even downloads go through this client, because a bare fetch inherits only the cookie and once exported the real graph while the person was viewing demo data.

steps.label: attach request id, start the timer
steps.note: The id is echoed as x-request-id and reappears in every error envelope, so a 500 in a log can be tied to the call that caused it.

steps.label: CSP nonce, Helmet headers, CORS allow-list
steps.note: script-src is nonce-based with strict-dynamic; frame-ancestors none. Inline styles and any HTTPS image/connect source are permitted: the soft edge of the policy.

steps.label: parse JSON body against the applicable limit
steps.note: The import parser is mounted at app.ts:51, ahead of the default at :52. A router-local parser would run too late: the 2 MB default rejects first (FR-010).

steps.label: 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE / 400 MALFORMED_JSON
steps.note: body-parser tags its errors; errorHandler maps entity.too.large, entity.parse.failed, encoding.unsupported and request.aborted explicitly rather than letting them reach the generic 500.

steps.label: enter the space and timezone AsyncLocalStorage scopes
steps.note: In Cloud mode spaceMiddleware deliberately ignores the browser-controlled x-vitae-space header and pins the legacy id until workspaceMiddleware replaces it.

steps.label: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED (no token) or UNAUTHORIZED (rejected)
steps.note: Three token paths are tried in cost order (local dev JWT, primary Firebase project, configured companion project), and DGM-AUTHENTICATION draws them. The refusal is written directly to the response, not thrown, and its message is neutral in every failure case so a probe holding a token learns nothing about why.

steps.label: resolve a member workspace for req.user.uid (Cloud only)
steps.note: Joins workspace_members to workspaces and workspace_lifecycles, and moves an expired trial or grace period to read_only in the same request. Skipped entirely when cloudEnabled() is false.

steps.label: 409 WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED, 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND, or 402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED
steps.note: The 404/409 pair comes from workspace resolution (workspace.ts:36-43); the 402 comes from the entitlement gate at workspace.ts:76. That gate is method-based, not route-annotated, so a route added without an annotation fails closed. Export, billing and logout stay reachable while read-only.

steps.label: run the rest of the request inside the workspace partition
validate the body, then open one transaction
steps.note: The route does its reads first (endpoint checks for every implied edge) before the first stage, so a write never half-lands on a missing reference.

steps.label: 422 VALIDATION with field-level detail
steps.note: ValidationError carries the parser's issue list; NotFoundError becomes 404; a thrown HttpError carries its own status and code.

steps.label: INSERT node + revision, scoped to space and workspace_id
steps.note: The partition is read from AsyncLocalStorage on every call rather than cached, which is what lets a maintenance script run inside an explicit partition with no request at all.

steps.label: committed; the in-process write generation and the search generation are bumped
steps.note: Memoised read models and the search index compare generations rather than guessing with a timer, so a value written a moment ago is visible on the next read. A failure to publish the invalidation is logged, never rethrown: the write is already committed and must not be reported as failed (repository.ts:650).

steps.label: 201 { node }
steps.note: On the way out, requestContext's finish handler logs the route pattern (not the raw path, which ids would shard), status and duration.

steps.label: { error: { code, message, details?, request_id } }
steps.note: One envelope for every failure. Anything unrecognised is logged with the request id and answered with a neutral 500.
